title: How to Transition From a Growth Portfolio to a Preservation Portfolio
description: The 'Glidepath' strategy for locking in your life's work.
content:
For 30 years, you were an 'Accumulator'. You bought stocks, ignored volatility, and chased growth. As you approach retirement, you become a 'Decumulator'. Your goal shifts from maximizing returns to ensuring the money lasts. This requires a fundamental shift in asset allocation—reducing 'Beta' (Volatility) and increasing 'Yield' (Cash Flow). This guide explains the 'Red Zone' transition strategy to land your portfolio safely.

Key Takeaways

  • The 'Red Zone': The 5 years before and after retirement are critical. You must reduce sequence of returns risk by shifting from 90% stocks to something more stable (e.g., 60/40 or 50/50).
  • Dividend Tilt: Shift from 'Growth' stocks (paying 0%) to 'Quality' or 'Dividend Growth' stocks (paying 2-3%). This provides cash flow to live on without selling principal.
  • Bond Laddering: Move from 'Total Bond Market' funds (which fluctuate) to 'Individual Bond Ladders' (which mature at par). This guarantees your paycheck.
  • Don't Abandon Growth: You still need 40-60% in equities to fight inflation for a 30-year retirement. Going to 100% cash guarantees you run out of money.

Why It Matters (US Context)

Target Date Funds do this automatically. If you are DIY, you must execute this glidepath yourself. Failure to de-risk before a crash (like 2000 or 2008) forces many seniors back to work.

The Allocation Shift

Move from offense to defense.

Phase 1: 5 Years Out (The Trim)

Old: 90% Stock / 10% Bond.
Action: Stop reinvesting dividends. Direct all new contributions to Bonds/Cash.
New: 75% Stock / 25% Bond.

Phase 2: 2 Years Out (The Tent)

Action: Sell volatile Tech/Small Cap stocks. Buy Short-Term Treasuries.
New: 60% Stock / 40% Bond.

Phase 3: Retirement Day (The Floor)

Action: Ensure you have 2 years of cash/liquidity.
New: 50% Stock / 40% Bond / 10% Cash.
Strategy: You are now crash-proof. You can live for 5+ years on the Bond/Cash side without selling a single stock.

Tax-Smart Moves

  1. Sell in Taxable: If you need to rebalance, sell High-Cost lots in your taxable account first (lowest tax hit). Or sell losers to harvest losses.
  2. Rebalance in IRA: Do the heavy lifting (selling $100k of stock to buy bonds) inside your IRA. There are no tax consequences for trading inside the shelter.
  3. Asset Location: Keep the new Bonds in the IRA. Keep the remaining Stocks in the Taxable account for tax efficiency.

Frequently Asked Questions

When do I go back to stocks?

The 'Rising Equity Glidepath' suggests that after the first 5-10 years of retirement (surviving the danger zone), you should actually increase stock exposure to fight late-life inflation.

Is 60/40 safe?

Historically, yes. It captures 70% of the upside with half the volatility. It is the standard for a reason.

What about Annuities?

Buying an annuity is the ultimate 'Preservation' move. You trade the asset for a guaranteed income stream. It fits the bond portion of the portfolio.
